title: EAL/2 with an installed finite-state checker
question: Can an EAL/2 argument coupled to a bounded model checker distinguish safe and unsafe supplied graphs and refuse mismatched evidence where authored structured support cannot?

scope.system_or_population: 48 generated finite directed graphs with at most eight states
scope.conditions: Fixed authored claim, explicit graph observation, inclusive horizon at most eight transitions and current EAL/2 semantics
scope.temporal_scope: One assessment per generated model at 2040-01-01T09:05:00Z
scope.exclusions: Physical plants, graph inference from sensors, arbitrary state spaces, model-authority authentication and model generation by an LLM
scope.knowledge_cut: 2026-09-23; earlier EAL/2 regression, relay and notation diagnostics are exposed development knowledge

claims.statement: For this fixed corpus, an EAL/2 argument with a registered checker and a matching recorded graph supports a bounded safety proposition exactly when an independent graph oracle finds no forbidden state within the horizon.
claims.scope_limit: The fixed 48 synthetic graphs and installed method implementation
claims.success_consequence: Demonstrate bounded integration and computed revision for this formal task
claims.failure_consequence: Reject the implementation-level claim and inspect mismatches

claims.statement: Mismatched scope and stale evidence cannot support the computed safety proposition in the tested host evaluation.
claims.scope_limit: The declared binding and freshness checks

claims.statement: A consistent but false graph supplied by a producer can still support the model-conditional safety proposition.
claims.success_consequence: Keep physical truth and authenticity outside the established claim
claims.failure_consequence: Investigate whether a separate authentication check exists

assumptions.statement: The reference enumerator implements paths of length zero through the inclusive horizon independently of the checker traversal.
assumptions.test_or_justification: Inspect the reference code and two hand-derived graphs before the matrix run

assumptions.statement: A supplied graph is a complete model for the formal property being assessed.
assumptions.test_or_justification: An explicit model assumption, deliberately not validated against a device

assumptions.statement: Matching record metadata identifies the intended acquisition but does not authenticate its producer.
assumptions.test_or_justification: Counterfeit-record control constructs internally consistent metadata around a false graph
assumptions.failure_consequence: The stated trust boundary needs revision

hypotheses.label: Computed conditional reasoning
hypotheses.statement: The checked EAL route agrees with an independent finite-graph oracle for all generated valid models and refuses all wrong-scope and stale controls.
hypotheses.scope: This deterministic corpus and EAL/2 version

hypotheses.label: Authored relation suffices
hypotheses.statement: A structured/1 author assertion using the same graph records distinguishes the safety property on this corpus as accurately as the computed route.
hypotheses.scope: Same graph and affirmative authored safety warrant

hypotheses.label: Trusted observation assumed
hypotheses.statement: Record correspondence alone rules out a false but internally consistent graph.

predictions.expected_pattern: All valid computed statuses agree with exhaustive paths; authored assertion supports unsafe models too
predictions.tolerance: Zero disagreements on the finite corpus

predictions.expected_pattern: All wrong-scope and stale records lose computed support
A false but coherently labelled safe graph is accepted as model-conditional support

constructs.name: bounded graph safety
constructs.definition: No path from start to any forbidden vertex with at most horizon directed edges
constructs.scope: Complete finite graph supplied to the method
validity_evidence: Independent path enumeration and hand cases
validity_threats: The represented graph may be incomplete or false about a physical system

measurements.observable: EAL claim status and independently enumerated path existence
measurements.instrument_or_procedure: Saved evaluator output and independent exact enumerator
measurements.timing: One fixed assessment per graph and arm
measurements.preprocessing: supported means safe; all other labels mean no positive support
measurements.calibration: Horizon-zero and direct-edge hand cases; all counterexample paths checked against edges
measurements.validity: Exact only for the supplied finite graph
measurements.measurement_invariance: Same source template, observation and horizon for paired arms
measurements.error_model: Implementation or oracle bug; no sampling noise
measurements.blinding: No analyst blinding; oracle computed before inspecting EAL outcomes

measurements.observable: Support status after changing only observation scope or age
measurements.error_model: Corrupted record digest would confound scope test; digest is recomputed

measurements.observable: Support on a falsified graph whose metadata and digest remain consistent
measurements.instrument_or_procedure: Replace a dangerous edge with a safe graph in one unsafe case
measurements.preprocessing: Compare model-conditional answer with the true held graph
measurements.calibration: Verify held graph unsafe and forged graph safe independently
measurements.error_model: The test itself is a controlled falsification

design.rationale: Finite exhaustive oracle can adjudicate a bounded computation; crossed safe/unsafe pairs reveal unchecked affirmative assertions
design.temporal_structure: Paired, one pass with fixed seed
design.assignment_method: Each generated model receives both routes; perturbations are applied after the base result
design.masking: Not applicable: automatic labels and fixed oracle
design.comparator: Same EAL graph record with structured/1 authored affirmative support

units.sampling_frame: 24 seeded safe graph families and each family's added forbidden transition
units.analysis_unit: Graph pair, with 48 records for the finite descriptive contrast
units.inclusion_criteria: Graphs with 6–8 vertices, a valid start, nonempty forbidden set and horizon 1–5
units.exclusion_criteria: None after generation; generator validity is checked before evaluation
units.recruitment_or_selection: Fixed pseudorandom seed 20260923 and deterministic pair construction

interventions_or_exposures.description: Replace structured authored support with a registered finite-state calculation and typed proposition binding
interventions_or_exposures.target: Inference from graph to bounded safety claim
off_target_checks: Graph payload, scope and claim text identical across routes

interventions_or_exposures.description: Perturb one observation scope or collection time at a time
interventions_or_exposures.implementation: Recompute the record value digest after scope change

controls.failure_mode_addressed: The checker might reject every claim
controls.implementation: Construct no incoming edge to the forbidden state

controls.description: 24 paired models with an added reachable forbidden edge
controls.failure_mode_addressed: The checker might support every claim
controls.implementation: Add one transition to forbidden within horizon

controls.failure_mode_addressed: Mistaking record binding for source authentication
controls.implementation: Replace one unsafe graph payload with its safe partner, recomputing the digest
controls.diagnostic_consequence: Support limits conclusions to the supplied model

confounds.description: The comparator omits a computation by definition
confounds.causal_or_measurement_path: It cannot infer safety from graph edges
confounds.control_or_adjustment: State comparison as an ablation of computation, not superiority over other solvers
confounds.diagnostic: Report standalone oracle as a credible alternative
confounds.residual_risk: The difference is expected from the chosen tasks

estimands.intervention_or_exposure: Registered checker plus EAL typed binding
estimands.summary_measure: Exact count and paired difference in oracle agreement

estimands.interpretation: Counterexample to claims of producer authentication

identification.causal_and_measurement_structure: The oracle enumerates graph paths; source and record are paired; only declared method or field changes within each contrast
identified_parameters: Exact outcomes on the fixed corpus
nonidentified_alternatives: Real-world safety, independent graph acquisition, model usability and superiority over another solver
threats: Common mistake in the two algorithms
rescue_actions: Correct fixture or independent oracle and rerun in a new result version

sampling.sample_size_or_information_target: 24 pairs, 48 graphs and 48 per-condition perturbations; exact finite description, no population interval
sampling.dependence_structure: The unsafe graph differs from its safe partner by one edge
sampling.multiplicity: One primary finite contrast, eligibility and counterfeit secondary
sampling.attrition_or_loss: Any missing or failed execution invalidates the complete-corpus criterion
sampling.sensitivity_analysis: One direct-edge and one horizon-zero hand case, and one counterfeit

analysis.preprocessing_lock: Generate seed-fixed graph pairs, oracle truth first, then run paired EAL routes

models.model_or_procedure: Exact counts and per-case retained paths/statuses
assumptions: Graph representation complete for the formal question
diagnostics: Reference path and reported path checked against graph

analysis.uncertainty: None for this fully specified finite corpus; no population inference
analysis.missing_data: Count incomplete and do not claim complete result
robustness_checks: Graph edge-order invariance on selected cases
analysis.inconclusive_handling: Retain failed inputs and do not elevate the primary claim

decision_matrix.observation_region: All 48 computed answers agree with the oracle, all controls pass and authored route supports all 24 unsafe graphs

claim_effects.rationale: The predeclared finite computational and eligibility observations match

hypothesis_effects: H-001 retained; H-002 contradicted for this ablation

risks.prevention: Predeclare the generator and finite inference
risks.detection: Report generator, cases and baseline behaviour
risks.sensitivity_or_correction: Test different topologies in a later study

bias_assessment.reporting_controls: Save all case-level outcomes, including failures
bias_assessment.residual_limitations: Synthetic author baseline and unvalidated physical graph

ethics_and_safety.stopping_rules: Stop if the oracle or method produces invalid state

feasibility.fallback: Run pure checker and oracle separately if host process execution fails; mark integration untested
